newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: HANSON SHOWS STRAIN OF CANNIBALISM CLAIM
Federal Independent MP Pauline Hanson has shown the strain of dealing with claims in her book that Aborigines were once canibals.
The canibalism claims in the book "Pauline Hanson - The Truth", have been widely criticised by Australian historians.
Ms Hanson became emotional when she told a packed meeting at Gatton west of Brisbane last night that she'd had a tough day dealing with the controversy.
Australian Reform Party Director and meeting organiser, Alan Spencer, says Ms Hanson pointed out that the material on cannibalism was researched by other people, and was not written by her.
NSW MINISTER TACKLES BANKS ON CHARGES
The Minister for Fair Trading is seeking an urgent meeting with bank managers in New South Wales, to talk to them about what she calls the banks' "rapacious greed"
Faye Lo Po says she's concerned about rising fees, and the decline in banking in rural areas.
She says she'll ask the banks what their future plans are for services in the bush.
Mrs Lo Po says she'll also to use her portfolio powers to beef up the contribution of credit unions to the banking sector.
TINGLE BLAMES GUN LOBBY FOR CONFRONTATION

Shooters' Party M-P John Tingle has complained to Premier Bob Carr about an incident yesterday in which the M-P was berated by one of the visiting Dunblane fathers in the foyer of the New South Wales Parliament.
Three of the fathers whose children were either killed or wounded in last year's Dunblane massacre in Scotland were in parliament to meet Mr Carr.
After the meeting Mr Tingle says one of the fathers grabbed his hand, berated him about his views on guns, thrust a picture of his dead daughter in his face and called him a murderer.
Mr Tingle says he understands the man's emotion, but claims the Coalition for Gun Control pointed him out to the Dunblane father, in a political stunt.
GAY GROUP CALLS FOR ACCESS TO I-V-F TREATMENT
The Australian Council for Lesbian and Gay Rights says bans on same sex couples using I-V-F treatment are out of step with community attitudes.
The Victorian Government has banned same-sex couples and single women from gaining access to infertility treatment.
But the Health Minister Rob Knowles will amend legislation to allow unmarried heterosexual couples access to the programs.
Robyn Walsh from Lesbian and Gay Rights Council says most people are either ambivalent towards same-sex couples using I-V-F programs, or feel the discrimination they experience is unfair.
PACKER MEETS HOWARD TO DISCUSS MEDIA LAWS
The fate of Australia's cross-media ownership laws is again under the spotlight, after a 90 minute meeting between the Prime Minister and media kingpin, Kerry Packer.
The law has consistently stymied the owner of the Nine Television Network in his attempts to seize control of the Fairfax Newspaper Group.
It's widely tipped that the Federal Government will scrap the laws when it finalises its review of media rules.
The law prevents television station owners from also controlling newspapers in the one city.
Mr Packer was making no comment on leaving his meeting with Mr Howard last night and Mr Howard's office said only that it was one of a series of meetings with media players.
